thesis: Agents are becoming a new privileged-identity class, and employee-account agents just inherited every permission a human never should have delegated.
why_now: This week's news shows the shift landing all at once: AI agents now run under employees' own accounts, and the OS is responding — Apple is tightening macOS Full Disk Access specifically because of agent risk.
evidence: Rig Security launches with $12M to watch AI agents that run under employees' accounts
Apple says it's tightening macOS 'Full Disk Access' controls due to new risks from AI agents
AI agent identity security demands layered defenses, Omdia says
angle: Don't build another scanner — build the runtime identity plane: per-agent scoped credentials, action-level attestation, and least-privilege shells that agents can't escape. The wedge is being the broker between the agent and every tool it touches, like an IAM layer purpose-built for non-human actors.

thesis: The inference war is over and the agent-infrastructure war just started: tokens are commoditized, so the money is moving to stateful 'full computers for agents'.
why_now: Modal is simultaneously raising a $750M round at $15.75B valuation, shipping GA clusters, and launching VM sandboxes pitched as 'full computers for agents' — while CoreWeave and NetApp/Nvidia reframe the bottleneck as wiring, power, and storage rather than raw FLOPs.
evidence: VM Sandboxes: Full computers for agents
Source: Inference provider Modal Labs closing in on $750M round at $15.75B valuation
Wiring and powering GPUs differently can swing AI latency by orders of magnitude, says CoreWeave
angle: Attack the agent-state layer: checkpoint/restore for long-running agent sessions, persistent memory and file systems, and reproducible sandbox images. Whoever owns cheap, instant, stateful agent sandboxes becomes the AWS-of-agents; the pure token API is a race to zero margin.

thesis: Orbital compute is splitting into two opposite bets — megawatt space data centers vs. inference on the satellite itself — and both need an orchestration layer that doesn't exist yet.
why_now: Google's own math says SpaceX needs 1,600 Starship launches before orbital data centers pencil out, while Satlyt just raised $8M to run AI models on satellites in orbit — the edge and the mega-DC are being built in parallel with no common software stack.
evidence: Google thinks SpaceX's Starship has to launch 1,600 times before space data centers get off the ground
Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
Satellite software provider Satlyt closes $8M investment
angle: Build the 'Kubernetes for orbit': a scheduler that handles radiation-hardened hardware, intermittent downlinks, thermal/power budgets, and workload migration between satellite edge and ground. Sell to the constellation operators who are all about to reinvent this wheel badly.
